ratings_why.fun: Every turn is a clock puzzle: which Vigil ends last for Brother Netopir, whether to go quiet for the Robber-Knight, and how to feed Mother Ribica's long count.
ratings_why.distinct: Countdowns plus a never-falling Dripstone total and an order-of-endings repeat play unlike any of today's tribes, though countdown units themselves are a known idea.

verdict_why: The Guild Knocker loop is a real fix; the rest is a strong design that should stay hot.

points.text: Knocker Vigils that count each other down can loop forever: three Knocker Vigils (one Knocker plus two Scribe copies), two golden ones, or two with the Seven-Year Sitter keep ending each other, and with Mother Ribica on board that is endless goldens. Cap it, e.g. a Vigil can end at most twice a turn, or Knocker count-downs can't end another Knocker Vigil.
It's unclear whether 'the lake' is one lake per Comes-and-Goes Olm or shared by all, and whether a Scribe copy or a second Olm gets its own. Say which; a shared lake is the more interesting puzzle.
'The numbers in their Vigil effects are doubled' needs a written rule (gold and stats yes, count-downs and 'a golden copy' no?), since it decides whether the Sitter feeds the Knocker loop.
The Flood-Mark Reader only reads Dripstone. Rewarding units whose Vigil ends next turn would add a timing choice and tie it to the clocks.
"Baby Dragon" is a pure Dripstone readout. Letting it count as a Dragon for the Dragon Under the Earth, or grow when another tribe's unit holds a lamp, would give it a second use.

standouts.why: Brother Netopir turns the order of endings into the real decision each turn, and Kurents and Parkelj change what ends last.
The Seven-Year Sitter flips the whole tribe from many small clocks to a few loud ones, and pairs with the Robber-Knight's quiet turns.
The Robber-Knight pays you to stop doing the tribe's main thing, so every turn asks whether this turn should be silent.

weakest.why: A flat Dripstone payoff that does one obvious job.
Reads one number and hits; no choice in how to play it.
Mostly a way to triple Olmlings; little interplay beyond that.

flags.note: Three Knocker Vigils, two golden ones, or two under the Sitter end each other with no end.
Any ending loop or Netopir repeat turns Ribica into many goldens in one turn.
+2/+2 per Dripstone on play is huge late, and counting as every tribe needs a rules check on each tribe.
Grows faster every turn since Dripstone never falls; check round 12+ totals.
Which numbers 'doubled' covers is not defined.
Whether the lake is shared or per unit is not stated.
